title: Silent, but not quiet
blurb: The silent era's loudest films. Stunts nobody would insure today, monsters that still work, and camera tricks that took eighty years to copy.

films.note: Keaton, a locomotive, and the most expensive single shot of the silent era. Nothing is faked.
The most complete cut. Max Schreck rising from the coffin still does it.
Douglas Fairbanks, a flying carpet, and sets the size of city blocks.
Lon Chaney's unmasking. Audiences screamed in 1925 and the makeup is still his.
Willis O'Brien's dinosaurs, eight years before he did King Kong.
The Odessa Steps. Every film school in the world starts here.
A day in the Soviet city, cut like nothing before it. No story, no intertitles, no equal.
A documentary about witchcraft that turns into the strangest horror film of its decade.
Fairbanks invents the swashbuckler. Watch him vault the furniture.
A clay giant brought to life in the Prague ghetto. The look Frankenstein borrowed.
John Barrymore's transformation, done with his face and no cuts.
Keaton versus the entire police force of Los Angeles. Eighteen minutes.
